item.title: C++ 'extern' Keyword for Global Variable Sharing Across Source Files
item.description:
“C++ ’extern’ Keyword for Global Variable Sharing Across Source Files”

Implementing Global Variable Sharing with extern

The mechanism for sharing variables globally across different source files hinges on the concept of linkage. The extern keyword is pivotal here, acting as a declaration that tells the compiler a variable exists but is defined elsewhere.

Method 1: Declaration in Header, Definition in One Source File

This approach is highly effective for variables intended for use everywhere. The header file communicates the existence and type of the variable, while one specific source file provides the definition (i.e., allocates memory for it).
